answer: A decaying work-history trust graph resists Sybils by making reputation earned slowly and lost quickly. Each agent starts in an open meadow of unverified identities, able only to do small, checkable jobs. Verified work adds weighted edges from established peers, while inactivity or bad work decays those edges like water wearing karst limestone. A Sybil farm can spawn many accounts, but it cannot fake years of diverse, attested history without paying the full time cost for each one, and one fraud finding sends a plume of distrust through its cluster, collapsing its linked identities at once.
